records.question: How does the policy define an Accident?
records.expected_answer: An Accident is a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, visible and violent means.

required_facts: The event is sudden, unforeseen and involuntary.
It is caused by external, visible and violent means.

evidence_spans.text: An Accident means sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, visible and violent means.

records.notes: Basic retrieval/control question.

records.question: What minimum duration qualifies as hospitalization, and can treatment under 24 hours qualify?
records.expected_answer: Inpatient care requires a stay of more than 24 hours. Treatment lasting under 24 hours can qualify as Day Care Treatment when it is medically necessary, is undertaken under general or local anaesthesia in a hospital/day-care centre in less than 24 hours because of technological advancement, and would otherwise have required hospitalization of more than 24 hours; ordinary outpatient treatment does not qualify.

required_facts: Inpatient care requires more than 24 hours in hospital.
Qualifying day-care treatment can take less than 24 hours because of technological advancement.
It must otherwise have required hospitalization for more than 24 hours and ordinary outpatient treatment is excluded.

evidence_spans.text: Inpatient Care means treatment for which the Insured Person has to stay in a Hospital for more than 24 hours for a covered event.

Day Care Treatment means Medical Treatment, and/or Surgical Procedure which is: i. undertaken under general or local anaesthesia in a Hospital/Day Care Centre in less than 24 hours because of technological advancement, and ii. which would have otherwise required Hospitalization of more than 24 hours. Treatment normally taken on an out-patient basis is not included in the scope of this definition.

records.notes: Tests general definition plus shorter-duration qualifying treatment.

records.question: Under what circumstances is domiciliary treatment covered?
records.expected_answer: Domiciliary treatment is covered when an illness would normally require hospital care but treatment occurs at home because the patient cannot be moved or no hospital room is available. The treatment must exceed three consecutive days, occur during the Policy Period, manage an illness rather than provide enteral feeding or end-of-life care, and the treating doctor must certify that the definition conditions are met.

required_facts: The illness would normally require hospital care but treatment occurs at home because the patient cannot be moved or a room is unavailable.
Treatment exceeds three consecutive days and is during the Policy Period.
It manages an illness and is not enteral feeding or end-of-life care.
Treating-doctor certification of the definition conditions is required.

evidence_spans.text: Domiciliary hospitalization means medical treatment for an Illness/disease/Injury which in the normal course would require care and treatment at a Hospital but is actually taken while confined at home under any of the following circumstances: i. the condition of the patient is such that he/she is not in a condition to be removed to a Hospital, or ii. the patient takes treatment at home on account of non-availability of room in a Hospital.

We will cover expenses related to Domiciliary hospitalization of the Insured Person if the treatment exceeds beyond three consecutive days and is availed during the Policy Period. The treatment must be for management of an Illness and not for enteral feedings or end of life care. At the time of claiming under this benefit, We shall require certification from the treating doctor fulfilling the conditions as mentioned under the general definitions (Section 1) of this Policy.

records.notes: Definition alone may be insufficient. Capture operative conditions.

records.question: How many days of pre- and post-hospitalization expenses are covered?
records.expected_answer: The policy covers up to 90 days of pre-hospitalization expenses and up to 90 days of post-hospitalization expenses, subject to an admitted claim under B1, B4 or B6.

required_facts: Pre-hospitalization coverage is up to 90 days before admission.
Post-hospitalization coverage is up to 90 days after discharge.
The benefit depends on an admitted B1, B4 or B6 claim.

evidence_spans.text: We will cover expenses for pre-hospitalization consultations, investigations and medicines incurred upto 90 days prior to the date of admission to the Hospital. Any pre-hospitalization expenses incurred prior to Policy Period shall not be covered. The benefit is payable if We have admitted a claim under B1, B4, or B6. We will cover expenses for post-hospitalization consultations, investigations and medicines incurred upto 90 days after discharge from the Hospital. The benefit is payable if We have admitted a claim under B1, B4, or B6.

records.notes: Deliberately straightforward retrieval control.

records.question: What happens if the insured chooses a room above the eligible room category?
records.expected_answer: The insured bears a rateable proportion of Room Rent and total Associated Medical Expenses (including surcharge or taxes), based on the difference between actual and entitled room rent divided by actual room rent. This deduction does not apply to ICU charges, hospitals without differential billing, or associated expenses not differentially billed by room category.

required_facts: A rateable deduction applies to Room Rent and total Associated Medical Expenses.
The proportion uses the difference between actual and entitled room rent divided by actual room rent.
ICU charges are exempt.
No proportional deduction applies where the hospital or expense does not use room-category differential billing.

evidence_spans.text: If the Insured Person is admitted in a room whose category is higher than the one that is specified in the Policy Schedule, then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the Room Rent and the total Associated Medical Expenses, including surcharge or taxes thereon in the proportion of the ‘difference between the Room Rent actually incurred & the Room Rent of the entitled room category’ to ‘the Room Rent actually incurred’. • Proportionate deductions are not applicable for ICU Charges. • Such proportionate deductions, if any, will not be applied in respect of the Hospitals which do not follow differential billing or for those Associated Medical Expenses in respect of which differential billing is not adopted based on the room category.

records.notes: Capture applicable deduction and material exceptions.

records.question: What expenses are covered and excluded for an organ donor?
records.expected_answer: The policy covers the donor’s medical expenses solely for harvesting an organ for the insured recipient when the donation complies with law, the recipient’s B1 surgery claim is accepted, the transplant is medically necessary, and assessment follows the recipient’s claim. It excludes the donor’s pre/post-hospitalization and screening expenses, other harvesting-related expenses or complications, acquisition costs, experimental/investigational transplants, and organ transport or preservation.

required_facts: Coverage is solely for harvesting the donated organ for the insured recipient.
The donation must comply with law, the recipient B1 claim must be accepted, and the transplant must be medically necessary.
Donor pre/post-hospitalization and screening expenses are excluded.
Other harvesting-related treatment/complications, acquisition costs, experimental transplants, and transport/preservation are excluded.

evidence_spans.text: We will cover the Medical Expenses, incurred by or in respect of the organ donor, for an organ transplant Surgery, solely towards the harvesting of the organ donated subject to the following conditions: i. The organ donation conforms to the Transplantation of Human Organs (Amendment) Bill, 2011 and the organ is for the use of the Insured Person; ii. The Insured Person is the recipient of the organ so donated by the organ donor and the claim of such Surgery is accepted by Us under B1 of this Policy; iii. The organ transplant is medically necessary for the Insured Person as certified by a Medical Practitioner iv. Claim under this section shall be assessed as per the claim of the recipient Insured Person What is not covered i. Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses or Post hospitalization Medical Expenses of the organ donor ii. Screening Expenses of the organ donor iii. Any other medical expense as a result of harvesting from the organ donor iv. Costs directly or indirectly associated with the acquisition of the donor’s organ v. Transplant of any organ/tissue where the transplant is experimental or investigational vi. Expenses related to organ transportation or preservation vii. Any other medical treatment or complication in respect of the donor, consequent to harvesting.

records.notes: Tests positive coverage plus exclusions.

records.question: What is the initial waiting period for illness and what are its exceptions?
records.expected_answer: Illness treatment is excluded for the first 30 days from first policy commencement. Covered accident claims are excepted, and the exclusion does not apply after more than 12 months of continuous coverage. The 30-day wait applies afresh to an enhanced Sum Insured.

required_facts: The initial illness waiting period is 30 days from first policy commencement.
Covered accident claims are excepted.
It does not apply where continuous coverage exceeds 12 months.
It applies to an enhanced Sum Insured.

evidence_spans.text: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident, provided the same are covered. This exclusion shall not, however, apply if the Insured Person has Continuous Coverage for more than twelve months. The within referred waiting period is made applicable to the enhanced Sum Insured in the event of granting higher Sum Insured subsequently.

records.notes: General rule plus material exceptions.

records.question: If cataract is also a pre-existing disease, which waiting period applies?
records.expected_answer: Cataract has a 24-month specified-disease waiting period, while a pre-existing disease has a 36-month waiting period. If the cataract is also pre-existing, the longer period applies: 36 months, subject to the policy’s continuity and disclosure terms.

required_facts: Cataract is a listed specified condition with a 24-month waiting period.
The PED waiting period is 36 months.
The longer waiting period applies when a specified disease is also pre-existing.

evidence_spans.text: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with Us.

Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with Us. If any of the specified disease/procedure falls under the waiting period specified for Pre-Existing Diseases, then the longer of the two waiting periods shall apply.
XVIII. Cataract (avrana Shukla), Retinal detachment, Glaucoma (abhishyandha)

records.notes: Tests interaction between specified-disease and PED waiting periods.

records.question: What is the maternity waiting period and how does the relevant option change it?
records.expected_answer: Maternity Care has a two-year continuous-coverage waiting period. If the Reduction of Maternity Care Waiting Period optional cover is purchased, it is reduced to one year of continuous coverage.

The optional reduction changes it to one year of continuous coverage.

records.question: How is the Favorable Experience Discount calculated?
records.expected_answer: At renewal, the discount is based on claim years in the last three policy years: three claim years 0%, two 5%, one 10%, and no claim 20%. A claim year is one in which at least one claim was paid, except a year with claims only under the named twin-sharing cash, multi-sharing cash, or Maternity Care benefits is not treated as a claim year for this calculation.

required_facts: The four bands are 3 years/0%, 2 years/5%, 1 year/10%, and no claim/20%.
A claim year is a policy year with one or more paid claims.
Claims only under the three named accommodation-cash/maternity benefits do not create a claim year for this calculation.

evidence_spans.text: At Renewal, the applicable Favorable Experience Discount will depend on below criteria: Claim Years in last 3 Policy Years Discount 3 Years 0% 2 Years 5% 1 Year 10% No Claim 20% Where ‘Claim Year’ is a Policy year in which one or more claim(s) have been paid. For the purpose of Favorable Experience Discount, a Policy year with claim only under ‘Daily Cash for choosing Twin Sharing Accommodation’, ‘Daily Cash for choosing Multi-Sharing Accommodation’ and ‘Maternity Care’ benefit will not be considered a ‘Claim Year’.

records.notes: Capture discount structure and material qualification.

records.question: What does Global Cover for Planned Hospitalization cover?

Covered foreign medical expenses are limited to inpatient and day-care hospitalization up to Sum Insured.
Claims are reimbursement-based, subject to possible case-by-case cashless arrangement.
Only balance basic Sum Insured and NCB, not restored Sum Insured, may be used.

evidence_spans.text: We will cover for Medical Expenses of the Insured Person incurred outside India, upto the sum insured, provided that the diagnosis was made in India and the insured travels abroad for treatment. The Medical Expenses payable shall be limited to Inpatient and daycare Hospitalization. Any claim under this cover can be made only on reimbursement basis.
